text.title: UI Component Library Basics Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on the token bridge, per-component file layout and public surface, DOM prop and ref forwarding, story coverage per state, and the two CI gates (axe + visual regression). Each is checkable against the package tree and the CI config.

rule.statement: Component styles MUST reference semantic token names exposed as CSS custom properties (`var(--color-surface-default)`, `var(--space-3)`). Literal hex colours, `rgb()` values and raw pixel spacing inside a component file are rejected — grep for `#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}` in the component directory MUST return zero hits.

rationale.source: Design-token practice / CSS custom property cascade

rule.rationale: A custom property resolves against the scope it is read in, so a theme or dark-mode class on an ancestor re-values every consumer at once. A literal cannot participate in that cascade, so a theme flip leaves islands of the old palette in exactly the components nobody re-audited — and those islands are invisible in the light theme where they were authored.

rule.statement: Each component occupies one directory containing `<Name>.tsx`, `<Name>.stories.tsx`, `<Name>.test.tsx` and `index.ts`. The package's `exports` map MUST expose only the barrel; consumer code MUST NOT deep-import internal file paths.

rationale.source: Node.js package `exports` field / library packaging practice

rule.rationale: Without an `exports` map every internal path is part of the public API by accident. A consumer that imports `dist/Button/Button.internal.js` turns an internal rename into a breaking change that no semver bump signals, because the maintainer had no way to know the path was load-bearing.

rule.statement: Every primitive wrapping a native element MUST spread `...rest` onto that element and forward its `ref` (via `forwardRef`, or the `ref`-as-prop form on React 19+). Hand-picking a prop allowlist is rejected.

rationale.source: React ref forwarding + WAI-ARIA attribute delivery

rule.rationale: Positioning libraries, focus managers and `react-hook-form`'s `register()` all need the DOM node; without a forwarded ref they attach to nothing and fail silently. A prop allowlist drops whatever the author did not anticipate — `aria-describedby`, `data-testid`, and most damagingly `type="submit"`, so the button renders correctly and stops submitting the form.

rule.statement: Each primitive MUST have a story for every variant crossed with every interaction state it supports: default, hover, focus-visible, disabled, loading, and error/invalid. States are forced via story parameters or `pseudo` decorators, not left to manual interaction.

rationale.source: Storybook / visual-regression tooling (Chromatic, Percy) capture model

rule.rationale: Snapshot tools diff only what a story renders. A state with no story is outside the baseline entirely, so a regression in the disabled or focus-visible appearance passes CI green — and those are precisely the states a token rename breaks first, because nobody looks at them by hand.

rule.statement: CI MUST run axe-core across every story (`@storybook/addon-a11y` with the test-runner, `@axe-core/playwright`, or `jest-axe`) and fail the build on any violation of impact `serious` or `critical`. A non-blocking report is not a gate.

rationale.source: Deque axe-core rule impact levels + WCAG machine-checkable subset

rule.rationale: axe detects only the machine-checkable subset of WCAG, but that subset — missing accessible name, insufficient contrast, invalid ARIA attribute combinations — is exactly the class of defect introduced mechanically by a token rename or a dropped prop. Gating there catches the regressions a human reviewer cannot see in a diff, while leaving the judgement calls (focus order, meaningful labels) to review.

rule.statement: Visual-regression baselines MUST be captured in a pinned environment: fixed browser version, fixed container image, fixed fonts (self-hosted, not system), fixed device-pixel-ratio and viewport. Baselines recorded on a developer machine are rejected.
rule.rationale: Font rasterisation and subpixel antialiasing differ between macOS and Linux, so an unpinned runner produces sub-threshold diffs on unrelated PRs. The team's response is always to raise the diff threshold or mute the check, at which point the gate exists in the config and nowhere else.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) exactly one application consumes the components and no second consumer is planned — ship them in-app and extract later; (b) an external design system (MUI, Mantine, Radix Themes) already covers the required surface, in which case build composition and theming on top rather than re-authoring primitives; (c) no design tokens exist yet and none are being defined — author the token set first, since a library built on literals cannot be retrofitted onto tokens without touching every file.
rule.rationale: A library is an API contract plus two CI gates. With a single consumer the contract costs a version-bump ceremony and buys nothing, because the only caller can be edited in the same commit as the change.
